extra.message: SQL Injection: The `create` method builds a SQL string via Python's `%` string formatting with user-controlled `name` parameter (from POST /students/ data['name']) before passing it to `cur.execute(q)`. The `'%(name)s'` is a Python format placeholder, not a SQL parameter, so the name is interpolated directly into the SQL string. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g., name = `x'); DROP TABLE students; --`). Should use parameterized queries: `cur.execute('INSERT INTO students (name) VALUES (%s)', (name,))`.

Missing Authorization: The `students` view's POST handler (creating a new student) lacks the `@authorize()` decorator. Although the HTML form is only displayed to authenticated users, the server endpoint accepts unauthenticated POST requests, allowing anyone to create arbitrary students (and exploiting the SQL injection in Student.create).

Missing Authorization: The `courses` view's POST handler (creating a new course) lacks the `@authorize()` decorator. Although the form is shown only to admins, the server endpoint does not require authentication or admin privileges, allowing any unauthenticated user to create courses.
Missing Authorization: The `review` view's POST handler (creating a course review) lacks the `@authorize()` decorator. Unauthenticated users can submit reviews, enabling stored XSS via review_text.

Missing Authorization: The `evaluate` view's POST handler (creating a mark/grade) lacks the `@authorize()` decorator. Although the form is only shown to admins, the endpoint accepts unauthenticated requests, allowing anyone to add grades to any student.

Weak Password Hashing: Passwords are hashed with raw MD5 (no salt, no key stretching). MD5 is cryptographically broken and trivially attacked with rainbow tables. The fixtures also store MD5 hashes (`md5('password')`, `md5('superadmin')`). Should use a slow, salted KDF such as bcrypt, scrypt, argon2, or PBKDF2.

extra.message: Jinja2 is configured with `autoescape=False`, disabling automatic HTML escaping for ALL templates. Combined with user-controlled data being rendered in templates, this enables multiple stored XSS vulnerabilities throughout the application (course reviews, course title/description, student name, etc.).

cwe: CWE-1188: Initialization of a Resource with an Insecure Default

extra.message: Stored XSS: `{{ review.review_text }}` renders the user-supplied review text without HTML escaping (`| e` filter missing) and autoescape is disabled. An attacker can post a review containing `<script>` tags or other HTML/JS payloads, which will execute in the browser of any user viewing the course page.

Stored XSS: `{{ course.title }}` renders user-supplied course title without escaping. Since autoescape is disabled, attacker-controlled course titles can inject HTML/JavaScript that executes in all visitors' browsers.
Stored XSS: `{{ course.description }}` renders user-supplied course description without escaping. Since autoescape is disabled, attacker-controlled descriptions can inject HTML/JavaScript.

Stored XSS: `{{ name }}` (in `{% for (id, name) in students %}`) renders user-supplied student name without escaping. Combined with the lack of authorization on the students POST endpoint and disabled autoescape, attackers can create students with names containing HTML/JS payloads that execute in any user's browser.
Stored XSS: `{{ course.title }}` rendered without `| e` filter in 'Write review to {course.title}'. An attacker can create a course with a malicious title that injects HTML/JS into this page.

Reflected/Stored XSS: `{{ fieldname }}: {{ errors }}` renders the validation error structure without escaping. The `fieldname` and `errors` may contain user-controlled content and are not escaped because autoescape is disabled.
Stored XSS: `{{ student.name }}` rendered without `| e` filter. Student name is user-controlled and not escaped (autoescape is disabled), enabling stored XSS in evaluation error pages.

Stored XSS: `{{ course.name }}` rendered without `| e` filter. Note: course has a `title`/`description` field (not `name`), so this is also a latent bug, but it would also be vulnerable to XSS if the field existed. The autoescape=False means even the `course.title` is unescaped on the evaluate page elsewhere (e.g., in the title block).

CSRF protection disabled: The `csrf_middleware` is defined in `sqli/middlewares.py` (and tokens are even generated via `csrf_processor` and embedded in all forms) but it is commented out in the middleware list. The line `# csrf_middleware,` (line 27) means CSRF tokens are never validated, making the application vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery on all state-changing endpoints.

Session cookie is created with `httponly=False`, allowing the session cookie to be accessed by client-side JavaScript. Combined with the XSS vulnerabilities in this application, an attacker can steal session cookies via `document.cookie` and impersonate users.

Debug Mode Enabled: The aiohttp Application is initialized with `debug=True`, which enables verbose tracebacks and exposes internals on errors. This can leak sensitive information such as source code, configuration values, environment variables, and stack frames to attackers.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Information Disclosure: The 500 error template renders `{{ error.__dict__ }}` directly to the page. This exposes all internal attributes of the HTTPException (and any exception propagated) including potentially headers, URLs, debug info, and message contents. The template also uses `{{ error.status }}` in `src="//http.cat/{{ error.status }}"` which is rendered without escaping (and status is normally an int, so not exploitable for XSS, but inconsistent).

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Hardcoded Database Credentials: The PostgreSQL password is hardcoded as `postgres` (with user `postgres`) in the committed `config/dev.yaml`. While this is the dev config, it is shipped in the repository and could be reused in production. Credentials should be loaded from a secret store or environment variables, not committed to source.

Hardcoded Weak Passwords in Fixtures: Test users are seeded with trivially weak passwords (`superadmin/superadmin`, `j.doe/password`, `s.king/password`, `p.parker/spidey`), stored as unsalted MD5 hashes. These credentials (and hashes) are committed to the repository and will be loaded into any deployment that runs the migrations, including production-like environments.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: Insecure Session Cookie Configuration: `RedisStorage` is created with only `httponly=False` and no `secure=True` or `samesite` argument. The session cookie is therefore not protected against MITM/session hijacking over HTTP, and lacks SameSite protection against CSRF (which is doubly important given CSRF middleware is disabled).
